root_cause.text: The `ethosu_gem_cmdstream_copy_and_validate()` function in the Arm Ethos-U NPU driver fails to validate that the incremented index `i` remains within the bounds of the `bocmds` buffer when processing a 64-bit command word, leading to an out-of-bounds write.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that in `drivers/accel/ethosu/ethosu_gem.c`, a check `if (i >= size / 4) return -EINVAL;` was added immediately after `i++` and before writing to `bocmds[i]` to prevent writing past the end of the buffer.

intent_record.how: Prevents an out-of-bounds write vulnerability by ensuring the index does not exceed the allocated buffer size.

This statement performs a write operation to the 'bocmds' buffer using the unvalidated, incremented index 'i', leading to a potential out-of-bounds write.

bic_trace_step.reason: In the function `ethosu_gem_cmdstream_copy_and_validate`, the loop iterates up to `size / 4`. When processing a 64-bit command word (indicated by `cmd & 0x4000`), the index `i` is incremented (`i++`) and used to write to `bocmds[i]` without checking if the incremented index exceeds the bounds of the `bocmds` buffer (which has `size / 4` elements). This allows an out-of-bounds write if the 64-bit command is at the very end of the stream.
